title: Runtime hotfix: session handle retention + allocator fragmentation causing cross-tenant GPU OOMs
creator: Ethan Walker
description: Multiple customer escalations over the past 36 hours (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) report abrupt GPU OOMs correlated with long-running chat sessions. Investigation indicates a compound failure: session handle retention across preemptions + tombstone buildup in the KV metadata index + slab allocator fragmentation. These together produce sudden address-space pressure and OOMs under realistic production traffic patterns.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start sustained chat workload with variable sequence lengths and repeated context swaps (prefix caching enabled).
2) Rapidly create and terminate high-concurrency interactive sessions to exercise session allocation paths.
3) Interleave model swaps (compatible variants) and preemptive eviction to trigger session handoff code paths.
4) Observe memory growth in GPU resident arenas and KV index tombstone count via mem dashboards (see links).
mitigations: Applied immediate throttling on affected host pools (hosted) to reduce burst allocation rates.
Enabled emergency per-tenant allocation caps on Dedicated nodes to prevent cross-tenant cascade.
Rolled a telemetry-only flag to garbage-collect stale session handles in a subset of clusters (non-destructive mode).
root_cause_summary: A race in session teardown allows session handles to persist after logical eviction; persistent handles keep tiny tensor arenas live and prevent KV tombstones from compacting. Over time, slabs become fragmented and free lists are starved, causing sudden OOM when a large allocation is requested. The KV index compaction path cannot reclaim when tombstone density passes a threshold because compaction uses synchronous locks that contend with the eviction queue under load.
proposed_fix: 1) Introduce a two-phase session fence: on preemption mark the session inert then asynchronously finalize handles (safe-evict fence). 2) Add incremental tombstone compaction (background, rate-limited) to the KV index with a lightweight backoff to avoid lock storms. 3) Partition allocator arenas by tenant affinity and add a fast-path reclaim for tiny arenas. 4) Add runtime flag to enable aggressive tombstone compaction for canary clusters only.
implementation_notes: Patch will touch runtime allocator (arena manager), session store, and KV index compactor. We will keep changes minimal and guarded by feature flags. The compactor uses an optimistic try-lock to avoid blocking latency-sensitive threads. The session fence uses epoch counters and a deferred cleanup worker so synchronous teardown work is bounded.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge runtime-1.29.2-hotfix branch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2742. 2) Canary deploy to staging and two low-traffic production clusters with telemetry flag enabled (72-hour soak). 3) Monitor OOM incidence, slab fragmentation metrics, tombstone density, and session handle counts. 4) Gradual rollout to Dedicated then Hosted then Private (customer-by-customer for on-prem). 5) If regressions, rollback by disabling flags and redeploying previous runtime image.
rollback_plan: Disable feature flags and redeploy runtime-1.29.1; if rollback fails, use node-level container restart with allocator priming disabled to ensure stable memory footprint.
qa_checks: Unit tests for session fence and deferred cleanup worker.
Integration test: sustained multi-tenant synthetic load reproducer should not diverge memory after 24h.
Performance benchmark: tail latency <= baseline+10% under canary config.
E2E: KV index tombstone density should decrease by >=60% in canary within 12h.
Chaos test: preemption and model swap storms do not leak live session handles.

Long-term: schedule allocator refactor in runtime-2.0 to remove slab fragmentation mode and improve multi-tenant isolation.
